newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine call money unchanged at 10.53125 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine call money unchanged at 10.53125 pct.

text.p: The Philippine interbank call loan rate was unchanged at 10.53125 percent despite weekend covering of banks, traders said.

"The market is still very liquid," one trader said, adding that banks were not reinvesting their maturing reverse repos due to low interest rates being offered by the Central Bank and a recent imposition of the 20 percent withholding tax.
Instead of investing in reverse repos, banks were looking at fixed-rate Treasury notes and commercial papers as alternative investment methods, he said.
Turnover was thin with 11.973 billion changing hands. Done rates hovered 1/32th percentage points above the Central Bank benchmark overnight borrowing rate of 10.5 percent.
The rate hit a high of 10.75 percent early in the session.
Banks usually borrow heavily on Mondays since they have to cover their reserve deficiencies since Friday.
The secondary market was quiet as banks were reluctant to sell their Treasury bills for fear that interest rates would go down further in this afternoon's auction.
Traders were expecting a further drop in T-bill rates due to excess liquidity in the market.
Secondary T-bill rates were mostly unchanged from Friday's quotes as banks await the T-bill results.
